label: Our manifesto
title: Risk is a movie.
description: We are building a connected understanding of financial life, so institutions can see how risk changes, act with greater clarity, and put capital to work with confidence.

sections.title: See the relationships.
sections.body:
A business exists within a network of customers, suppliers, owners, accounts, and obligations. A household’s financial position reflects income, commitments, and the timing of both. An isolated record can tell us something important. Understanding how it connects to other records can change what it means.

Our mission begins with mapping those connections. An invoice, a processor settlement, and a bank deposit may describe different stages of the same economic event. Resolving that relationship helps prevent double counting and makes the underlying activity easier to understand. It also helps teams distinguish an established connection from one that still needs investigation.

We believe a useful risk graph must preserve the evidence behind every relationship. Its value comes from helping a team ask better questions: who is connected, through what activity, over which period, and with what degree of certainty?

sections.title: Follow the financial life.
sections.body:
Risk unfolds over time. A strong month can sit inside a weakening trend. A temporary disruption can occur in an otherwise resilient business. The same balance can mean different things depending on when it was observed, what came before it, and which obligations come next.

We believe an assessment should carry its time and context with it. Teams need to know what was available when a decision was made, what has changed since, and whether the change warrants another look. New evidence should build on the history of a relationship while preserving the original assessment for review.

This is what we mean when we say risk is a movie. Monitoring should make the story easier to follow, with a clear account of source freshness, gaps in coverage, and the limits of what can currently be observed.

sections.title: Keep the evidence in view.
sections.body:
An insight is more useful when someone can examine how it was reached. A team should be able to trace an observation to its source, understand the calculation or interpretation behind it, and see what remains unresolved. Evidence, inference, and judgment each have a place in a decision. Their differences should stay visible.

We believe missing information deserves an explicit place in an assessment. Conflicting records, uncertain entity matches, incomplete periods, and stale connections can materially change an interpretation. A polished output should make those limitations easier to see. Confidence must be supported by what the evidence can actually establish.

That belief shapes our approach to risk intelligence: preserve provenance, expose assumptions, make calculations reproducible, and give reviewers a clear path back to the underlying record. The goal is understanding that can survive a serious question.

sections.title: Understand the opportunity.
sections.body:
Capital allocation involves understanding both exposure and possibility. A business may have reliable receipts despite an irregular billing cycle. A borrower may have capacity that becomes clearer when income, expenses, and obligations are considered together. Better context can reveal questions worth pursuing and opportunities worth understanding.

Our ambition is to help institutions distinguish uncertainty that can be investigated from risk they are prepared to accept. A useful assessment should explain the sources of resilience as carefully as the sources of concern. It should support decisions about structure, timing, capacity, and the conditions that require review.

Improving access to capital starts with improving the quality of understanding behind it. Each institution sets its own appetite and policies. We want teams to have the evidence to apply those policies thoughtfully and consistently, with a clearer view of the customer and the opportunity.

sections.title: Strengthen human judgment.
sections.body:
AI can help teams read records, reconcile information, investigate inconsistencies, and prepare evidence for review. Specialized agents can take on defined analytical work within an institution’s workflow. Their contribution should be visible enough for a person to challenge, correct, or reject.

We believe authority must be explicit. A model’s output, a policy check, a recommendation, and a final decision are different steps. Teams need clear review points, meaningful exceptions, and a record of how responsibility moved through the process. The institution retains control of lending decisions, customer communication, and intervention.

The measure of useful automation is the quality of the work it enables people to do. We want analysts to spend more time resolving important questions, applying experience, and exercising judgment. Technology should give them a stronger basis for taking responsibility for the answer.

sections.title: Carry context through the lifecycle.
sections.body:
The work of understanding a customer should remain useful after an approval. Verification establishes evidence. Underwriting interprets capacity and obligations. Monitoring follows changes. Servicing and review decisions draw on the history of the relationship. Each stage benefits from knowing what the previous stage established and what it left open.

We believe the original assessment should provide a clear baseline for what comes next. When permitted new evidence arrives, teams should be able to examine it against that baseline and understand why a reassessment may be needed. A change in circumstances should be connected to the reasoning that supported the earlier decision.

This is the continuity we are building toward: financial understanding that travels with the relationship. Amlok’s role is to support that understanding across the credit lifecycle, while institutions and their operational systems remain responsible for executing the actions they approve.

sections.title: Connect with permission.
sections.body:
Financial evidence comes with responsibilities to the people and businesses it describes. Mapping an ecosystem requires disciplined boundaries around what can be accessed, why it is needed, who can use it, and how long it should be retained. Broader understanding must be earned through appropriate permission and careful handling.

We believe every deployment should make data access, intended use, and accountability clear. Access for a particular assessment does not by itself authorize unrelated reuse, sharing between institutions, or model training. Those purposes require their own explicit basis and agreed controls.

The same care applies to interpretation. Financial patterns can reflect differences in context and coverage. Institutions should examine whether the evidence and methods are appropriate for the population and decision at hand. Respect for the customer belongs in the design of the workflow, from collection through review.

sections.title: Earn trust through measurement.
sections.body:
An ambitious vision needs rigorous evaluation. We believe every performance claim should be tied to a defined task, a documented dataset, a meaningful baseline, and a clear account of its limits. A result becomes useful when others can understand how it was produced and where it may fail.

Financial research requires particular care with time. Evaluation should respect what was knowable at the point of decision, keep future information out of historical inputs, and examine performance across relevant segments. Retrospective findings can inform a deployment. Prospective observation and ongoing review are needed to understand how a system behaves in use.

Our commitment is to state the scope of our research precisely. Evidence from extraction, retrieval, or a structured prediction task supports conclusions about that task. Broader claims about financial understanding require their own evidence. We intend to keep testing assumptions, documenting limitations, and improving the system as we learn.

sections.title: Build infrastructure that fits.
sections.body:
Financial institutions have systems, policies, teams, and customer relationships that already carry responsibility. Risk intelligence should be able to join that environment through clear interfaces and dependable handoffs. Adoption should have a defined purpose, a reviewable scope, and an understandable path into production.

We believe teams should be able to start with a concrete problem: organizing an underwriting file, resolving conflicting evidence, or reviewing a change after funding. They should be able to inspect the result, establish the controls they need, and expand the role of the technology as its usefulness is demonstrated.

That is why we think in terms of infrastructure. APIs, connected evidence, repeatable assessments, and observable workflows give institutions building blocks they can use within their own operating model. The aim is intelligence that remains useful as products, policies, and customer needs evolve.

sections.title: Put understanding to work.
sections.body:
The purpose of better risk intelligence reaches beyond producing a score or completing a file. Capital supports livelihoods, businesses, and long-term plans. The systems that inform its allocation should help institutions understand those real circumstances with greater care and clarity.

We want a future in which a team can investigate an opportunity without repeatedly assembling its history from scratch; in which a changing relationship can be reviewed with its original context intact; and in which a question about risk can be answered with evidence that people can examine.

This future will be built through research, practical deployment, and sustained collaboration with the institutions that serve customers. Our role is to make financial relationships more understandable and the reasoning around them more useful. Our purpose remains improving how capital is accessed, allocated, and managed.

steps.title: Review changing conditions

label: API reference
title: One API.
description: A documented resource model for connecting sources, assessing risk, monitoring changes and tracing evidence.

sections.title: Shared infrastructure
sections.body: Manage authorized subjects, connections and normalized information before initiating product workflows. Provider coverage and permissions determine which data is available.

sections.title: Insights and Signal
sections.body: Initiate underwriting, retrieve immutable analysis outputs, activate monitoring and inspect alerts. Preserve returned IDs and trace material results to their input evidence.

sections.title: Build against a precise contract
sections.body: Use the OpenAPI 3.1 document and current reference for schemas, scopes, errors and examples. Pin the version your integration supports and review changes before release.

label: SDKs & developer tools
title: The right tools.
description: Start with OpenAPI, runnable examples and signature verification helpers for Node.js and Python.

sections.title: A contract you can build on
sections.body: Download the OpenAPI 3.1 contract for resource schemas, authentication and operation definitions. Use the contract with your preferred client tooling and validate the generated behavior against your environment.

sections.title: Explore with Postman
sections.body: Import requests grouped by product domain and configure your institution-issued base URL. Synthetic saved responses help you understand the shape of a request before connecting live data.

sections.title: Language examples and helpers
sections.body: Follow cURL, Node.js fetch and Python requests examples. The maintained webhook helpers verify raw-body signatures; your integration adds persistence, deduplication and processing. These tools are examples and helpers rather than packaged Amlok SDKs.

label: Webhooks
title: When the evidence changes,
description: Receive changes as events, verify their origin and retrieve the authoritative resource when your workflow needs it.

sections.title: Subscribe to meaningful changes
sections.body: Register an approved HTTPS destination and choose event types from the catalog. Store the destination signing secret when it is issued and keep it separate from the API key.

sections.title: Verify, persist, then acknowledge
sections.body: Validate the signature against the exact request bytes. Accept events into a durable inbox before returning success, and process them asynchronously with workspace-aware deduplication.

sections.title: Recover without repeating work
sections.body: Delivery can arrive more than once or out of order. Inspect event history and delivery attempts, reconcile newer resource versions, and replay retained events while preserving their original identity.

label: MCP integration
title: Connect your AI tools
description: Design an MCP integration around authorized Amlok resources, scoped tools and the evidence behind each result.

sections.title: Make the boundary explicit
sections.body: An MCP server can expose selected API operations to an AI client. Start with approved read-only resources and a clear mapping between the user, workspace and permitted action.

sections.title: Keep authority in the application
sections.body: Use least-privilege credentials on the server and validate every resource request. Separate retrieving evidence from starting a workflow or changing monitoring configuration.

sections.title: Plan your Amlok connection
sections.body: Review the API contract and your intended AI workflow with the team. Server availability, deployment and supported operations are confirmed for your integration.

label: Integration prompt
title: A better brief.
description: A focused integration brief grounded in the Amlok contract, your environment and production-ready handling.

sections.title: Provide the source of truth
sections.body: Ask your agent to read the current OpenAPI contract and relevant product journey before writing code. Supply your framework and intended workflow without sharing live credentials.

sections.title: Make the behavior concrete
sections.body: Include scope checks, asynchronous state handling, idempotent retries, signed webhooks and evidence retrieval. Request tests for missing permission, expired authorization and duplicate delivery.

sections.title: Review before enabling live data
sections.body: Have an engineer verify the generated integration against the provisioned sandbox, permissions and business requirements. Keep decisions and consequential actions under your institution’s control.

label: Sandbox
title: Test the journey.
description: Exercise underwriting and monitoring with provisioned synthetic records, realistic state changes and test credits.

sections.title: A separate place to build
sections.body: Your account manager provides sandbox access and a fixture pack. Authorized administrators create a sandbox key and select scenarios through the client portal.

sections.title: Test outcomes, not only responses
sections.body: Complete an Insights assessment or a Signal monitoring journey. Check returned evidence, resulting resource IDs, usage records and alerts against the scenario’s expected state.

sections.title: Prepare for the edges
sections.body: Exercise expired authorization, insufficient credits, rejected evidence, workload limits, retryable failures and duplicate deliveries. Reset fixtures in the sandbox before a deliberately fresh test.

label: Agent Skills
title: Make integration knowledge
description: Package the right references, checks and workflow instructions so your team’s agents work from the same foundation.

sections.title: Capture the integration playbook
sections.body: A skill can bundle task instructions with links to the API contract, product journey and security requirements. Keep it focused on a specific task such as implementing signed webhook delivery.

sections.title: Ground the work in current references
sections.body: Include the documentation index and require the agent to resolve actual operations and schemas before it writes code. Keep secrets and borrower data outside the skill.

sections.title: Keep review part of the workflow
sections.body: Require a sandbox verification checklist, evidence of expected behavior and human review before production. Reusable guidance helps teams stay consistent without granting an agent new authority.

label: Changelog
title: Keep your integration
description: Follow the current contract and compatibility guidance when adopting changes to your Amlok integration.

sections.title: Current documented reference
sections.body: The integration onboarding guide identifies Amlok API 1.4.2. The downloadable contract provides the current operation and schema definitions.

sections.title: Treat versions separately
sections.body: API paths, schema revisions, resource versions and policy versions serve different purposes. Read the compatibility guide before updating a client or interpreting changed outputs.

sections.title: A deliberate release process
sections.body: Pin the contract used by your integration, review changed fields and capabilities, rerun sandbox checks, and confirm environment-specific details with your Amlok contact.

label: Service status
title: Service health
description: Check live website and documentation availability, find the status reference for your Amlok environment, and reach support when a workflow is affected.

sections.title: Read the service report
sections.body: Request /v1/service-status from your institution-issued Amlok API URL. The endpoint does not require an API key. Inspect the overall status, each service’s status, and the updated_at observation time. A successful HTTP response means the report was retrieved, not that every service is operational.

sections.title: Check the workflow as well
sections.body: Treat unknown, stale, or unreachable status as unconfirmed availability. A healthy API does not by itself confirm a completed assessment, fresh provider data, or a delivered webhook. Check the state and source coverage of the affected resource as well.

sections.title: Report an incident
sections.body: Contact support@amlok.io or your agreed incident channel with the affected environment, impact, time window, request IDs, and redacted diagnostics. Follow your support agreement for incident severity, coverage, and escalation.

label: Security & compliance
title: Trust belongs
description: Security, privacy, and governance designed into the workflow. Review the controls and responsibilities that apply to your deployment.

sections.title: Protect the full processing boundary
sections.body: Encryption, scoped access and tenant separation support the protection of financial information. Confirm data locations, provider roles, retention and support access for the deployment you intend to use.

sections.title: Evidence for your review
sections.body: Amlok’s security program aligns controls with SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria and ISO/IEC 27001 principles. Scoped assurance materials and applicable provider reports are available for review under NDA.

sections.title: Keep decisions accountable
sections.body: Define intended use, validate outputs against representative data and retain the evidence behind material results. Your institution sets lending policy, reviews exceptions and owns consequential decisions.

sections.title: Agree responsibilities early
sections.body: Before connecting live data, establish source permissions, permitted processing, access ownership, escalation contacts and retention. The signed agreement records the responsibilities for your deployment.

label: Privacy
title: Privacy Policy
description: How Amlok handles website enquiries, booking information, and authorized institutional processing, including retention and privacy requests.

sections.title: Purpose-limited processing
sections.body: Amlok processes information for the agreed underwriting and monitoring workflows. Institutions define permitted purposes and source permissions; processing responsibilities are documented in their agreements.

sections.title: Information you provide
sections.body: When you contact Amlok, the information you choose to send is used to respond to your request. Send only what is needed and use an approved secure channel when sensitive material is required.

sections.title: Connected financial information
sections.body: Customer deployments can process authorized account information, financial records, documents, identity attributes and analysis outputs. The actual categories, providers and processing locations depend on the agreed service.

sections.title: Retention, access and requests
sections.body: Workspace retention is configured for the applicable purpose and requirements. Account cancellation and workspace deletion follow the documented process. Contact privacy@amlok.io for privacy questions or rights requests.

sections.title: Application and enterprise policies
sections.body: The published application privacy policy describes collection, consent, rights and cross-border processing for the Amlok web application. Enterprise processing instructions are governed by the applicable agreement.

label: Cookies & preferences
title: Cookies Policy
description: Learn about Amlok website language storage, Cal.com scheduling, external services, and browser controls.

sections.title: Your language preference
sections.body: This website stores your selected language in your browser’s local storage using the key amlok-language. The preference remains in that browser until you change it or clear the site’s stored data.

sections.title: Control stored data
sections.body: You can remove local storage and cookies through your browser’s site-data settings. Clearing this website’s stored preference returns it to its default selection.

sections.title: Links and external services
sections.body: Documentation, social profiles, AI summary services and other linked websites have their own storage and privacy practices. Visiting those services brings their policies into scope.

sections.title: Website and application
sections.body: The marketing website and authenticated Amlok application are separate experiences. The application’s published privacy and security policies describe its session and data-handling practices.

label: Terms of business
title: Terms of Business
description: Website use, service agreements, authorized processing, billing, cancellation, and responsibilities for an Amlok relationship.

sections.title: Your service agreement
sections.body: The signed agreement defines the services, usage rates, workload limits, commitments and responsibilities applicable to your institution. Published product information supports evaluation and does not replace those agreed terms.

sections.title: Authorized use and access
sections.body: Your institution authorizes users, protects credentials and establishes permissions for the information it provides. Keep underwriting and monitoring within the intended workflows and approved data sources.

sections.title: Usage and billing
sections.body: Insights and Signal draw from one shared credit balance. Usage charges, negotiated terms, payment methods and account controls follow the relevant rate card and agreement.

sections.title: Decisions and shared responsibility
sections.body: Amlok provides risk intelligence and evidence. Your institution owns its lending policies, review procedures, borrower communications and final decisions.

sections.title: Questions about your agreement
sections.body: Contact support@amlok.io or your dedicated account manager to discuss service scope, billing, renewal, cancellation or a contractual requirement.

sections.title: Photography and asset credits
sections.body: Team photography: Amlok. Provider and partner marks belong to their respective owners. Additional asset and software attributions are available in the website’s third-party notices.

label: Amlok vs Prism Data
title: Amlok and
description: Prism Data turns bank transaction history into cash-flow scores and financial attributes. Amlok combines authorized evidence with underwriting workflows and ongoing risk reassessment. There is overlap in credit intelligence; the practical choice depends on whether you need a specialist score, a connected assessment workflow, or both.

comparison.summary: Prism Data turns bank transaction history into cash-flow scores and financial attributes. Amlok combines authorized evidence with underwriting workflows and ongoing risk reassessment. There is overlap in credit intelligence; the practical choice depends on whether you need a specialist score, a connected assessment workflow, or both.
vendorStrengths: CashScore provides credit-risk and first-party-fraud predictions derived from deposit-account activity.
Dedicated products cover transaction categorization, income assessment, and financial attributes.
CashScore accepts data through aggregators, decision engines, or an API, with reason information for credit decisions.
amlokFit: Combine permitted bank, accounting, commerce, and lender-system evidence around the same subject.
Use Insights for an underwriting assessment and Signal for changes against an approved monitoring baseline.
Preserve source records, derived attributes, and workflow evidence in a common data model.
considerations: Compare outputs on your portfolio: a specialist score, an assessment snapshot, and a monitoring alert solve different parts of the process.
Evaluate coverage, model validation, reason information, and permitted use for your institution and market.
Both can sit within a wider lending architecture. A combined deployment requires confirmed data access, technical compatibility, and commercial terms; no direct integration is implied.

label: Amlok vs Flinks
title: Amlok and
description: Flinks provides bank connectivity, document verification, enriched financial insights, and payment infrastructure. Amlok uses authorized evidence to support underwriting and continued risk assessment. The products overlap in financial analysis, while connectivity and risk workflow needs can also be complementary.

comparison.summary: Flinks provides bank connectivity, document verification, enriched financial insights, and payment infrastructure. vendorStrengths: Flinks Connect supports financial-account data access, while Upload verifies financial documents.
Enrich analyzes income, cash flow, liabilities, and financial behaviour, with API, webhook, and dashboard access.
Flinks also offers account-to-account payments and managed open-banking services.
amlokFit: Bring approved evidence from several business systems into a consistent assessment context.
Retrieve an underwriting result with its frozen evidence, then monitor subsequent change.
Send result and alert notifications into institutional systems through signed webhooks.
considerations: Separate the requirements for connecting accounts, analyzing data, assessing risk, and moving money before comparing scope.
Amlok supplies risk information; borrower funding, payment controls, and institutional intervention remain in the lender's authorized systems.
Validate the specific bank, geography, consent, history, refresh cadence, and integration route. An integration catalog entry is not universal production coverage.

label: Amlok vs JUDI.AI
title: Amlok and
description: JUDI.AI focuses on small-business lending for community financial institutions, combining borrower applications, cash-flow underwriting, and configurable lending workflows. Amlok focuses on connected risk intelligence and assessment workflows. They overlap in underwriting, with different implications for the institution's application experience and operating systems.

comparison.summary: JUDI.AI focuses on small-business lending for community financial institutions, combining borrower applications, cash-flow underwriting, and configurable lending workflows. Amlok focuses on connected risk intelligence and assessment workflows. They overlap in underwriting, with different implications for the institution's application experience and operating systems.
vendorStrengths: A digital small-business application and review workflow can operate alongside an existing LOS or serve as the small-business LOS.
Its credit model uses bank transaction data and categorization to assess business cash flow.
Configurable branding, application forms, policies, document handling, and annual review workflows support lending operations.
amlokFit: Analyze business evidence across financial accounts and approved operational sources.
Connect verification, underwriting, monitoring, and investigation within authorized assessment workflows.
Keep lending decisions and borrower interventions with the institution's existing teams and systems.
considerations: Start with your operating model: a small-business lending application platform and an intelligence layer are not identical purchases.
Test relevant loan types, borrower segments, available data, model explanations, and workflow controls using your own evaluation criteria.
If considering both products, confirm the supported handoff and integration effort. Do not assume an out-of-the-box JUDI.AI–Amlok connection.

label: Amlok vs Covaleyo
title: Amlok and
description: Covaleyo combines loan-origination software with Covarity's commercial loan monitoring. Amlok connects underwriting evidence and ongoing risk signals. There is overlap in monitoring, while an LOS, borrowing-base platform, and risk-intelligence layer can serve different roles within the same institution.

comparison.category: Loan origination and commercial portfolio monitoring
comparison.summary: Covaleyo combines loan-origination software with Covarity's commercial loan monitoring. Amlok connects underwriting evidence and ongoing risk signals. There is overlap in monitoring, while an LOS, borrowing-base platform, and risk-intelligence layer can serve different roles within the same institution.
vendorStrengths: Origination tools cover application capture, configurable adjudication, approvals, and connections to lending systems.
Covarity supports covenant calculations, borrowing-base automation, and commercial portfolio review.
Borrower document collection, review workflows, and activity histories support repeatable monitoring operations.
amlokFit: Normalize authorized provider and lender records while retaining their source evidence.
Combine an assessment baseline with new evidence to identify material changes in borrower risk.
Deliver alerts and supporting information for the institution to review and act on.
considerations: If covenant administration, borrowing-base certificates, or application processing are central requirements, evaluate those workflows explicitly.
Amlok is not presented as a replacement for all LOS, loan administration, or borrower-servicing functions.
For a combined architecture, map the system of record, evidence ownership, alert handoffs, and access controls before planning an integration.

label: Amlok vs Intellifi / Nesto Cloud
title: Amlok and
description: Intellifi's official website now identifies the business as Nesto Cloud. Its current offering spans residential and commercial lending technology, including origination, underwriting, servicing, and operational delivery. Amlok provides risk intelligence within the credit lifecycle, which can complement operational platforms rather than replace every function they perform.

comparison.summary: Intellifi's official website now identifies the business as Nesto Cloud. Its current offering spans residential and commercial lending technology, including origination, underwriting, servicing, and operational delivery. Amlok provides risk intelligence within the credit lifecycle, which can complement operational platforms rather than replace every function they perform.
vendorStrengths: Residential tools cover acquisition, applications, adjudication, underwriting, funding, and servicing.
Commercial offerings address origination, underwriting, servicing, and asset management.
Institutions can evaluate SaaS delivery alongside outsourced lending operations supported by lending specialists.
amlokFit: Connect risk assessments to the institution's authorized evidence and existing operating model.
Use monitoring results to inform portfolio review and institutional intervention.
Keep consistent source records and explicit data-availability boundaries across connected systems.
considerations: Compare operational scope first. A mortgage origination or servicing replacement involves functions beyond an intelligence API.
Confirm current Nesto Cloud branding, module availability, and delivery model during evaluation; some published commercial portal features are marked coming soon.
Amlok does not collect borrower repayments or administer payment promises. Complementary use depends on a confirmed integration and clear operational responsibility.

label: Amlok vs Inverité Insights
title: Amlok and
description: Inverité brings together identity checks, bank verification, enriched financial data, and risk models. Amlok combines authorized evidence into underwriting and monitoring workflows. Both address risk assessment; the relevant comparison is the data, outputs, and workflow responsibility each supplies for your institution.

comparison.category: Identity, bank verification, and financial risk signals
comparison.summary: Inverité brings together identity checks, bank verification, enriched financial data, and risk models. Amlok combines authorized evidence into underwriting and monitoring workflows. Both address risk assessment; the relevant comparison is the data, outputs, and workflow responsibility each supplies for your institution.
vendorStrengths: ID Verify and Bank Verify address identity, account ownership, income, and financial activity.
Enrich organizes permissioned transaction data into income, spending, cash-flow, and behaviour information.
Default IQ and bespoke models support risk signals, while Micro Check addresses lending-history and off-bureau indicators.
amlokFit: Use a common evidence model across approved financial and business data sources.
Coordinate included verification and investigation stages within an authorized Insights or Signal workflow.
Connect initial assessments with monitoring while preserving institutional decision ownership.
considerations: Evaluate identity, bank-data access, enrichment, predictive outputs, and ongoing monitoring as separate requirements.
Ask each provider to demonstrate data coverage, explanations, consent handling, and validation against the borrowers you actually serve.
There is direct overlap in intelligence, and there may be complementary data roles. Any combined deployment requires verified availability and integration terms.
